title: The Stone Release and the Value a Piece Is Carried At
content:
# Care, Custody and Control Bulletin: The Release and the Value a Piece Is Carried At

## What the release settles

The release a customer signs for a piece the bench of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service has in hand names the value the chain carries that piece at while it holds it, and that value is worked out from the papers standing on the piece rather than from the figure taken down over the counter.

Once the release stands signed, the work order shows both the signed release and the agreed figure, and the customer can see both on their own copy of the work order.

## Who signs it

The release is the customer's to sign. The desk unlocks the workshop's own tool `confirm_stone_release_3a8d360e` and hands it over to be run by the customer themselves, since consenting to the chain working on stones it did not supply is theirs alone to give.

One call marks the release as signed on the named work order and writes onto that same order the value the piece is held at while the chain has it, replacing whatever figure was taken down over the counter.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `service_order_id` | the bench work order record the release is signed against | an id, as returned by the work order lookup |
| `customer_id` | the customer profile signing the release | an id, as returned by the customer profile lookup |
| `carried_value` | the value the piece is held at while the chain has it | USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half to even at the cent, always positive and never abbreviated to whole dollars |

### Return

A one-line confirmation naming the work order the release was signed against and the value now standing on it in USD to two decimal places. A returned line that repeats that figure is the receipt that the release stands signed and the order carries the agreed value.
